trends.name: Agent engineering emphasizes portable skills and persistent memory
trends.summary: Several open-source tools provide cross-session memory and skill libraries, and Pydantic AI has released Pax, a pluggable terminal coding agent.
trends.attention_driver: Demand for long-task stability and cross-model migration is driving the componentization of skills, memory and execution orchestration.

evidence.quote: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent
evidence.claim: Supports the claim that developers are adding persistent cross-session context for multiple types of agents.

evidence.quote: 一切皆插件，支持 --agent 接入自定义 Pydantic AI Agent
evidence.claim: Supports the claim that terminal coding agents are adopting pluggable agent access methods.

evidence.quote: Custom Skills let you package domain expertise and organizational knowledge.
evidence.claim: Supports the claim that skill packages are used to encapsulate organizational knowledge and reuse it in agent workflows.

trends.so_what: Design skill packages and session memory as replaceable layers to avoid locking workflows into a single model or coding assistant. Evaluate based on task completion rates and recovery capability.

trends.name: Enterprise agents add a business semantics layer
trends.summary: Reports say OpenAI is building the Athena semantic layer for ChatGPT Work to unify business metric definitions and reduce data agent guesswork.
trends.attention_driver: Errors by data analysis agents have exposed product gaps in metric definitions and permission management.

evidence.quote: OpenAI's data agent in ChatGPT Work still isn't accurate enough.
evidence.claim: Supports the claim that OpenAI is reportedly using a semantic layer to reduce errors in data agents' business understanding.

evidence.quote: OpenAI要给GPT做个“翻译官”，让智能体更懂业务
evidence.claim: Supports the claim that Athena is described as a data management layer that helps agents understand enterprise business semantics.

trends.so_what: For agents that work with business data, make metric definitions and permissions product-layer capabilities first. Model upgrades cannot replace this determinism.

trends.name: Verifiable mathematical reasoning becomes a test of capability
trends.summary: Discussion around AI mathematical proofs focuses on the speed of proof generation and the importance of formal verification with Lean and Mathlib.
trends.attention_driver: When complex outputs can be verified by independent systems, improvements in model capability can more readily accumulate into trusted work results.

evidence.quote: The Lean and Mathlib communities have verified that the proof is correc
evidence.claim: Supports the claim that the related mathematical proof has been reported as verified by the formal tools community.

evidence.quote: AI's recent math breakthroughs matter far be
evidence.claim: Supports the claim that the industry is focusing on AI systems' ability to continuously produce mathematical results.

evidence.quote: Math Proofs Are Landing Faster Than We Can Read Them
evidence.claim: Supports the claim that the speed of mathematical proof generation has become a topic of ongoing recent discussion.

trends.so_what: In high-value tasks that can be formally verified, product opportunities depend more on verification workbenches and evidence presentation than on whether a model gets the answer right in one attempt. Include human review time and reproducibility in evaluation.

insights.text: Agent reliability depends on external layers: memory, business semantics and verifiable results are becoming key conditions for products to complete tasks
Verification interfaces become a product differentiator: for independently verifiable tasks, build the evidence chain and recovery process into the workflow
